sentences.zh: ◎二郭兩王張牛

translations.literal: ◎ The Two Guos, Two Wangs, Zhang, and Niu
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Biographies: The Two Guos, the Two Wangs, Zhang, and Niu

sentences.zh: =郭虔瓘=

translations.literal: = Guo Qianzhen =
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qianzhen

sentences.zh: 郭虔瓘，齊州歷城人。

translations.literal: Guo Qianzhen was a man of Licheng in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qianzhen was a native of Licheng in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 開元初，錄軍閥，遷累右衛驍將軍，兼北庭都護、金山道副大總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he was entered in the military registers, and through successive promotions became General of the Valiant Cavalry of the Right Guard, concurrently serving as Protector-General of Beiting and Vice Grand Commander of the Jingshan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign he was enrolled as a military officer and rose through successive posts to General of the Valiant Cavalry of the Right Guard, while also holding the posts of Protector-General of Beiting and deputy grand commander of the Jingshan circuit.

sentences.zh: 明年，突厥默啜子同俄特勒圍北庭，虔瓘飭壘自守。

translations.literal: The next year Tong'e Tegin, son of the Türk qaghan Mojilian, besieged Beiting; Qianzhen strengthened the ramparts and held his ground.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Tong'e Tegin, son of the Türk qaghan Mojilian, laid siege to Beiting, and Qianzhen fortified the walls and defended the city.

sentences.zh: 同俄單騎馳城下，勇士狙道左突斬之。

translations.literal: Tong'e rode alone to the foot of the walls; a brave man lay in ambush to the left of the road, rushed out, and cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: Tong'e came alone on horseback to the foot of the wall, where a brave soldier ambushed him from the left of the road, charged out, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 虜亡酋長，相率丐降，請悉軍中所資贖同俄死，聞已斬，舉軍慟哭去。

translations.literal: The enemy had lost their chieftain; they came forward in groups to beg surrender, asking to use all the supplies in the army to ransom Tong'e's life; when they heard he had already been executed, the whole army wailed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: With their leader dead, the enemy came forward in groups to surrender, offering all the supplies they carried to ransom Tong'e's life; when they learned he had already been killed, the entire force broke into mourning and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 虔瓘以功授冠軍大將軍、安西副大都護，封潞國公。

translations.literal: For his merit Qianzhen was appointed Champion Grand General and Vice Protector-General of Anxi, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement Qianzhen was made Champion Grand General and Vice Protector-General of Anxi, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 建募關中兵萬人擊餘寇，遂前功，有詔募士給公乘，在所續食。

translations.literal: He proposed recruiting ten thousand troops from Guanzhong to attack the remaining bandits and carry forward his earlier achievements; an edict ordered recruiting soldiers, granting them gongcheng rank, with continued rations at their stations.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed raising ten thousand men from Guanzhong to pursue the remaining rebels and build on his earlier success; the court ordered recruitment, granted recruits the rank of gongcheng, and supplied continued rations wherever they were posted.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠韋湊上言：「漢徙豪族以實關中，今畿輔戶口逋耗，異時戎虜入盜，丁壯悉行，不宜更募驍勇，以空京甸，資荒服。

translations.literal: The Director of Palace Construction Wei Cou submitted a memorial: "The Han relocated powerful clans to fill Guanzhong; now the population of the capital region is depleted and scattered. When in the past the barbarians raided, every able-bodied man was sent away. It is not fitting to recruit more fierce warriors, emptying the capital district to supply distant frontier regions.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cou, Director of Palace Construction, memorialized: "The Han moved great families into Guanzhong to strengthen the heartland; today the capital districts are losing people. Whenever the frontier tribes raid, every able-bodied man is marched away. We should not recruit more elite troops and strip the capital plain bare to feed remote border commands.

sentences.zh: 萬人所過，遞馱熟饔，亙六千里，州縣安所供億？

translations.literal: Where ten thousand men pass, relay teams carry cooked provisions for six thousand li—how are the prefectures and counties to supply it all?
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand men on the march require relay trains of hot meals across six thousand li—where are the prefectures and counties to find the supplies?

sentences.zh: 秦、隴以西，多沙磧，少居人，若何而濟？

translations.literal: West of Qin and Long there is mostly sandy desert, with few inhabitants—how is such a force to be sustained?
translations.idiomatic: West of Qin and Long lies mostly sandy waste, with few settlers—how can an army be fed there?

sentences.zh: 縱有克獲，其補幾何？

translations.literal: Even if there were victories, how much would they make up for?
translations.idiomatic: Even if there were victories, how much would they offset the cost?

sentences.zh: 儻稽天誅，則諉大事。」

translations.literal: If Heaven's punishment should be delayed, the great enterprise will be blamed on others."
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven withholds success, the blame will fall on the whole undertaking."

sentences.zh: 不省。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 既而虔瓘果不見虜，還，遷涼州刺史、河西節度大使，進右威衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Before long Qianzhen, as predicted, found no enemy; he returned and was transferred to Governor of Liangzhou and Grand Commissioner of the Hexi Circuit, advancing to General of the Right Weiwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: As Wei Cou had warned, Qianzhen found no enemy and returned; he was then made governor of Liangzhou and grand commissioner of the Hexi circuit, and promoted to general of the Right Weiwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 四年，奏家奴八人有戰功，求為遊擊將軍，宰相劾其恃功亂綱紀，不可聽，罷之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized that eight household slaves had merit in battle and asked that they be made Mobile Corps generals; the chief ministers impeached him for relying on merit to disrupt discipline, and the request was denied and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he asked that eight household slaves who had fought well be appointed mobile-corps generals; the chief ministers charged him with using his record of service to overturn proper order, the request was refused, and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 陜王為安西都護，詔虔瓘為副。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shan was made Protector-General of Anxi, and Qianzhen was ordered to serve as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shan became Protector-General of Anxi, Qianzhen was appointed his deputy.

sentences.zh: 虔瓘與安撫招慰十姓可汗使阿史那獻數持異，交訴諸朝。

translations.literal: Qianzhen and Ashina Xian, commissioner for pacification and consolation of the Ten Surnames khans, repeatedly differed in their views and lodged mutual accusations at court.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhen and Ashina Xian, the commissioner charged with pacifying the Ten Surnames khans, clashed repeatedly and kept filing complaints against each other at court.

sentences.zh: 玄宗遣左衛中郎將王惠賫詔書諭解曰：「朕聞師克在和，不在眾，以虔瓘、獻宿將，當舍嫌窒隙，戮力國家。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong sent Wang Hui of the Left Guard Central Commandant's office with an edict to instruct and reconcile them, saying: "I have heard that armies conquer through harmony, not numbers. As veteran generals, Qianzhen and Xian should set aside suspicion and rancor and devote their strength to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong sent Wang Hui, a central commandant of the Left Guard, with an edict of reconciliation: "I have heard that victory comes from unity, not head count. You are seasoned commanders; put aside your grudges and serve the realm together.

sentences.zh: 自開西鎮，列諸軍，戍有定區，軍有常額，卿等所統，蕃漢雜之，在乎善用，何必加募？

translations.literal: Since the western garrisons were opened, armies have been arrayed, garrisons have fixed districts, and forces have regular quotas. Those you command mix barbarian and Han troops—the matter lies in using them well; why must you add recruitment?
translations.idiomatic: Since the western commands were established, each army has its zone and fixed establishment; the forces under you mix tribal and Han troops. Use them well—why keep asking for more recruits?

sentences.zh: 或云突騎施圍石城，獻所致也；

translations.literal: Some say the Turgesh siege of Shicheng was brought about by Xian;
translations.idiomatic: Some blame Xian for the Turgesh siege of Shicheng;

sentences.zh: 葛邏祿稱兵，虔瓘所沮也。

translations.literal: others say the Qarluk raising of arms was thwarted by Qianzhen.
translations.idiomatic: others credit Qianzhen with checking the Qarluk when they took up arms.

sentences.zh: 大將不協，小人以逞，何功可圖？

translations.literal: When great generals are not in accord, petty men take their chance—what achievement can be sought?
translations.idiomatic: When senior commanders feud, petty men profit—what merit can you hope to win?

sentences.zh: 昔相如能詘廉頗，寇恂不吝賈復，宜各曠然，終承朕命。

translations.literal: In former times Xiang Ru was able to yield to Lian Po, and Kou Xun did not begrudge Jia Fu—you should each open your hearts and in the end accept my command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Ru once humbled himself before Lian Po, and Kou Xun did not begrudge Jia Fu; open your hearts to each other and carry out my orders to the end.

sentences.zh: 今賜帛二千段及他珍器，俾諒朕意。」

translations.literal: Now I bestow two thousand bolts of silk and other precious objects, that you may understand my intent."
translations.idiomatic: I now send you two thousand bolts of silk and other fine gifts, so you may know my mind."

sentences.zh: 虔瓘奉詔。

translations.literal: Qianzhen received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhen accepted the edict.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒軍中。

translations.literal: After a long while he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 以張孝嵩為安西副都護。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaosong was appointed Vice Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaosong was made Vice Protector-General of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 孝嵩，偉姿貌，及進士第，而慷慨好兵。

translations.literal: Xiaosong had a imposing stature and passed the jinshi examination, yet was bold-spirited and fond of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosong was imposing in appearance, had passed the jinshi examination, and was ardent and drawn to military life.

sentences.zh: 在安西勸田訓士，府庫盈饒。

translations.literal: In Anxi he encouraged farming and trained troops, and the storehouses were full.
translations.idiomatic: In Anxi he promoted farming and drilled the troops until the granaries overflowed.

sentences.zh: 徙太原尹，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Taiyuan and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to governor of Taiyuan, where he died.

sentences.zh: 以黃門侍郎杜暹代。

translations.literal: Du Xian, Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xian of the Secretariat replaced him.

sentences.zh: 郭知運

translations.literal: = Guo Zhiyun =
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhiyun

sentences.zh: 郭知運，字逢時，瓜州晉昌人。

translations.literal: Guo Zhiyun, courtesy name Fengshi, was a man of Jinchang in Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhiyun, whose courtesy name was Fengshi, came from Jinchang in Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 長七尺，猿臂虎口，以格鬥功累補秦州三度府果毅。

translations.literal: He stood seven feet tall, with long arms and tiger's-mouth hands; for prowess in hand-to-hand combat he was repeatedly appointed garrison commander of the third degree in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet tall, with long arms and powerful hands; for his skill in close combat he rose through repeated appointments as a third-rank garrison commander in Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 從郭虔瓘破突厥有功，加右驍衛將軍，封介休縣公。

translations.literal: Following Guo Qianzhen he had merit in defeating the Turks and was promoted to General of the Right Xiaowei Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Jiexiu County.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Guo Qianzhen against the Turks, he distinguished himself and was made a general of the Right Xiaowei Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiexiu.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃將坌達延、乞力徐寇渭源，盜牧馬，詔知運與薛訥、王晙等相掎角，敗之。

translations.literal: The Tibetan generals Bendayan and Qilixu raided Weiyuan and stole pasture horses; Zhiyun was ordered to coordinate with Xue Ne, Wang Jun, and others in pincer attacks and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetan generals Bendayan and Qilixu raided Weiyuan and drove off the pasture horses, Zhiyun was ordered to join Xue Ne, Wang Jun, and others in a coordinated attack and rout them.

sentences.zh: 進階冠軍大將軍，兼臨洮軍使，封太原郡公，賜賚萬計。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Champion Grand General, concurrently made commander of the Lintao Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery, and rewarded with gifts numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Champion Grand General, made commander of the Lintao army as well, enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan, and showered with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 徙隴右諸軍節度大使、鄯州都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Commissioner of the Longyou Armies and Governor of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand commissioner of the Longyou armies and governor of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥降戶阿悉爛、𨁂跌思泰率眾叛，執單于副都護張知運，詔以朔方兵追擊，至黑山呼延谷敗之，虜棄伏走，取副都護還。

translations.literal: The surrendered Türk households of Ashilan and Tiediesitai led their followers in revolt and seized Vice Protector of the Chanyu Court Zhang Zhiyun; an edict ordered pursuit with Shuofang troops; at Huyan Valley on Black Mountain they were defeated, the enemy abandoned their ambush and fled, and the vice protector was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When the surrendered Türks Ashilan and Tiediesitai rebelled and seized Vice Protector Zhang Zhiyun of the Chanyu court, Zhiyun was ordered to pursue with Shuofang troops; at Huyan Valley on Black Mountain he routed them, the rebels abandoned their ambush and fled, and Zhang was rescued.

sentences.zh: 詔知運兼隴右經略使，營柳城。

translations.literal: An edict made Zhiyun concurrently Longyou frontier commissioner and ordered him to build up Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Longyou frontier commissioner and ordered to establish a base at Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，大破吐蕃，獻俘京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he inflicted a great defeat on Tibet and presented captives in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 5 he won a major victory over Tibet and presented prisoners in the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，復出，將輕兵丙夜至九曲，獲精甲、名馬、牦牛甚眾。

translations.literal: The next year he went out again, leading light troops at the third watch of the night to Jiugu, and seized a great quantity of fine armor, famous horses, and yaks.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he marched out again with light troops, reaching Jiugu in the dead of night and capturing large stores of fine armor, prized horses, and yaks.

sentences.zh: 既獻獲，詔分賜文武五品以上清官及朝集使三品者。

translations.literal: After the spoils were presented, an edict ordered them distributed among civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above who held pure offices, and among assembly commissioners of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: After the booty was presented at court, an edict divided it among fifth-rank and higher civil and military officials in pure posts and among third-rank provincial assembly commissioners.

sentences.zh: 進兼鴻臚卿，攝御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was advanced to concurrent Minister of Ceremonial and acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Minister of Ceremonial and acting censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 六州胡康待賓反，率王晙討平之。

translations.literal: Kang Daibin of the Six Prefectures Hu rebelled; leading Wang Jun he suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Daibin of the Six Prefectures Hu rebelled, he led Wang Jun to crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 拜左武衛大將軍，授一子官，賜金帛。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Left Wuwei Guard, one son was granted an office, and he was rewarded with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the Left Wuwei Guard; one of his sons received an official post, and he was rewarded with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒於軍，年五十五，贈涼州都督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died in the army at age fifty-five; posthumously he was made Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died on campaign at fifty-five; posthumously he was made governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 知運屯西方，戎夷畏憚，與王君㚟功名略等，時號「王郭」。

translations.literal: Zhiyun was stationed in the west, and the frontier tribes feared him; his fame was roughly equal to Wang Jun'ou's, and the age called them "Wang and Guo."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyun held the western frontier, where the tribes feared him; his renown matched Wang Jun'ou's, and contemporaries spoke of them together as "Wang and Guo."

sentences.zh: 帝詔中書令張說紀其功於墓碑。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Chief Minister Zhang Yue to record his achievements on a tomb stele.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Chief Minister Zhang Yue inscribe his achievements on a tomb stele.

sentences.zh: 上元中，配饗太公廟。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he was given a place in the sacrifices at the Taigong Temple.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan reign he was granted a share in sacrifices at the Temple of the Grand Duke.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，謚曰威。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongtai he was given the posthumous title Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongtai era he received the posthumous name Wei.

sentences.zh: 子英傑、英乂。

translations.literal: His sons were Yingjie and Yingyi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yingjie and Yingyi.

sentences.zh: 知運子 英傑英傑，字孟武，為左衛將軍、幽州副總管。

translations.literal: Zhiyun's son Yingjie—Yingjie, courtesy name Mengwu—was General of the Left Guard and Vice Commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyun's son Yingjie, courtesy name Mengwu, served as a general of the Left Guard and vice commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，長史薛楚玉遣英傑與裨將吳克勤、烏知義、羅守忠帥萬騎及奚眾討契丹，屯榆關。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan the chief administrator Xue Chuyu sent Yingjie with subordinate generals Wu Keqin, Wu Zhiyi, and Luo Shouzhong to lead ten thousand cavalry and Xi tribesmen against the Khitan, encamping at Yuguan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 the chief administrator Xue Chuyu sent Yingjie with the subordinate generals Wu Keqin, Wu Zhiyi, and Luo Shouzhong at the head of ten thousand horsemen and Xi allies against the Khitan, encamping at Yuguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 契丹酋長可突於拒戰都山下，奚眾貳，官軍不利，知義、守忠引麾下遁去，英傑、克勤力戰死。

translations.literal: The Khitan chieftain Ketuyu resisted battle below Dushan; the Xi turned traitor and the government army fared badly; Zhiyi and Shouzhong led their followers in flight, while Yingjie and Keqin fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan leader Ketuyu gave battle below Mount Du; the Xi defected, the imperial force was beaten, Zhiyi and Shouzhong fled with their men, and Yingjie and Keqin were killed fighting to the end.

sentences.zh: 其下尚六千人，殊死戰，虜示以英傑首，終不屈，師遂殲。

translations.literal: His remaining six thousand men fought to the death; the enemy displayed Yingjie's head, yet they would not yield, and the army was annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand of his men still fought to the death; when the enemy showed them Yingjie's head they still refused to submit, and the force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 知運子 英乂英乂，字元武，以武勇有名河、隴間，累遷諸衛員外將軍。

translations.literal: Zhiyun's son Yingyi—Yingyi, courtesy name Yuanwu—was famed between the Yellow River and Longyou for martial valor and rose through repeated appointments as outside general of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyun's son Yingyi, courtesy name Yuanwu, won fame between the Yellow River and Longyou for courage in battle and rose through posts as outside general of the guards.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰見之曰：「是當代吾節制者。」

translations.literal: Geshu Han saw him and said: "This man will one day take my place as frontier commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han said of him, "This is the man who will succeed me as frontier commissioner."

sentences.zh: 祿山亂，拜秦州都督、隴右采訪使。

translations.literal: When the Lushan rebellion broke out he was appointed Governor of Qinzhou and Longyou investigation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion erupted he was made governor of Qinzhou and Longyou investigation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊將高嵩擁兵入汧、隴，英乂偽勞之，且具饗，既而伏兵發，盡虜其眾。

translations.literal: The rebel general Gao Song led troops into Qian and Long; Yingyi feigned welcoming them with a feast prepared, then ambush troops sprang up and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel general Gao Song marched into Qian and Long, Yingyi pretended to welcome him with a banquet, then sprang an ambush and took his entire force prisoner.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，加隴右節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was additionally made military commissioner of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 2 he was also made military commissioner of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 召還，改羽林軍大將軍，掌衛兵。

translations.literal: He was recalled and changed to Grand General of the Imperial Forest Army, in charge of the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made grand general of the Imperial Forest Army and put in charge of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 以喪去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 史思明陷洛陽，謀掠陳、蔡，詔英乂統淮南節度兵。

translations.literal: Shi Siming took Luoyang and planned to raid Chen and Cai; Yingyi was ordered to command the Huainan circuit troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming seized Luoyang and planned to ravage Chen and Cai, Yingyi was ordered to take command of the Huainan circuit armies.

sentences.zh: 賊叩陜、虢，又改陜西節度、潼關防禦使。

translations.literal: When the rebels threatened Shan and Guo he was again changed to Shanxi circuit commissioner and defender of Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels pressed Shan and Guo, he was reassigned as Shanxi circuit commissioner and defender of Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 進御史大夫，兼神策軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Censor-in-Chief and concurrently made military commissioner of the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-chief and also made military commissioner of the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，以檢校戶部尚書兼大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong acceded he was made Acting Minister of Revenue while retaining the post of Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong came to the throne, Yingyi was made acting minister of revenue while keeping the post of censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 雍王率諸將討賊洛陽，留英乂殿於陜。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yong led the generals to attack the rebels at Luoyang, leaving Yingyi to hold the rear at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yong led the generals against the rebels at Luoyang and left Yingyi to hold Shan in the rear.

sentences.zh: 東都平，權知留守，無檢御才，其麾下與朔方、回紇遂大掠都城及鄭、汝，環千里無居人。

translations.literal: When the eastern capital was pacified he was made acting defender; he lacked the talent to restrain them, and his subordinates together with the Shuofang and Uyghur forces then plundered the capital and Zheng and Ru, so that for a thousand li around there were no inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern capital was recovered he served as acting defender, but he could not control his men; together with the Shuofang and Uyghur troops they looted the capital and the Zheng and Ru regions until no one lived within a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 以功實封三百戶，召拜尚書右僕射，封定襄郡王。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted three hundred actual households in fief, recalled and appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed as Prince of Dingxiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received a fief of three hundred households, was recalled as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed as Prince of Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 日驕蹇，為侈汰。

translations.literal: Day by day he grew arrogant and overbearing, and his conduct was extravagant and wasteful.
translations.idiomatic: He grew daily more arrogant and extravagant.

sentences.zh: 陰事宰相元載以久其權。

translations.literal: In secret he curried favor with the chief minister Yuan Zai to prolong his power.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly cultivated Chief Minister Yuan Zai to keep his power.

sentences.zh: 未幾，嚴武死成都，乃拜劍南節度使。

translations.literal: Before long Yan Wu died at Chengdu, and Yingyi was appointed military commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yan Wu died at Chengdu, and Yingyi was made military commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 自以有內主，故肆志無所憚。

translations.literal: He considered himself to have a patron within the palace, and therefore gave free rein to his will without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Believing he had a powerful patron at court, he acted without restraint.

sentences.zh: 初，玄宗在蜀時舊宮為道士祠，冶金作帝象，盡繪乘輿侍衛，每尹至，先拜祠，後視事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xuanzong was in Shu, his former palace had become a Daoist shrine; metal was cast into an image of the emperor, and imperial carriages and attendants were fully painted; whenever a prefect arrived he would first bow at the shrine, then conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong had been in Shu, his former palace had become a Daoist temple with a cast-metal image of the emperor and painted scenes of the imperial train; every new prefect would worship there before taking up office.

sentences.zh: 英乂愛其地勝選，輒壞繪像自居之，眾始不平。

translations.literal: Yingyi admired the site's fine location and choice views, and promptly destroyed the painted images to live there himself; the people first grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi coveted the fine site, tore down the painted images, and moved in himself—the first sign of public anger.

sentences.zh: 又教女伎乘驢擊球，鈿鞍寶勒及它服用，日無慮數萬費，以資倡樂，未嘗問民間事，為政苛暴，人以目相謂。

translations.literal: He also taught female performers to play polo on donkeys; inlaid saddles, jeweled bridles, and other attire cost tens of thousands each day to support singing girls and musicians; he never inquired into the people's affairs, and his government was harsh and cruel—people exchanged glances in warning.
translations.idiomatic: He had female entertainers play polo on donkeys; inlaid saddles, jeweled bridles, and other luxuries cost tens of thousands a day to sustain singers and musicians. He never troubled himself with the people's affairs, ruled with harsh cruelty, and people warned one another with glances alone.

sentences.zh: 怨崔寧不己同也，出兵襲寧，不克。

translations.literal: He resented Cui Ning for not siding with him and sent troops to attack Ning, but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Angry that Cui Ning would not join him, he marched against Ning and failed.

sentences.zh: 寧因人之怨，率麾下五千直搗成都。

translations.literal: Ning, relying on the people's resentment, led five thousand of his followers straight against Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the tide of popular resentment, Ning led five thousand men straight at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 英乂拒戰，眾皆反戈內攻，乃奔簡州，次靈池，普州刺史韓澄斬首送寧，遂屠其家。

translations.literal: Yingyi resisted battle, but his men all turned their weapons inward against him; he fled to Jianzhou and halted at Lingchi; Han Cheng, governor of Puzhou, cut off his head and sent it to Ning, who then slaughtered his family.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi tried to fight, but his own troops turned on him; he fled to Jianzhou and stopped at Lingchi, where Han Cheng, governor of Puzhou, beheaded him and sent the head to Ning, who then massacred his family.

sentences.zh: 王君㚟

translations.literal: = Wang Jun'ou =
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun'ou

sentences.zh: 王君㚟，字威明，瓜州常樂人。

translations.literal: Wang Jun'ou, courtesy name Weiming, was a man of Changle in Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun'ou, whose courtesy name was Weiming, came from Changle in Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 初事郭知運為別奏，累功至右衛副率。

translations.literal: At first he served Guo Zhiyun as a personal attendant, and through accumulated merit rose to Deputy Commander of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a personal attendant to Guo Zhiyun and rose through merit to deputy commander of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 知運卒，代為河西隴右節度使、右羽林軍將軍，判涼州都督事。

translations.literal: When Zhiyun died he replaced him as military commissioner of Hexi and Longyou and General of the Right Yulin Army, acting as Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhiyun's death he succeeded him as military commissioner of Hexi and Longyou, general of the Right Yulin Army, and acting governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元十四年，吐蕃酋悉諾邏寇大斗拔谷，君㚟間其怠，率秦州都督張景順乘冰度青海襲破之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan the Tibetan chieftain Sinuoluo raided Dadoubagu; Jun'ou seized on their slackness and led Qinzhou Governor Zhang Jingshun across the ice over Qinghai Lake in a surprise attack that broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 14 the Tibetan leader Sinuoluo raided Dadoubagu; Jun'ou caught them off guard and, with Qinzhou governor Zhang Jingshun, crossed the frozen Qinghai Lake in a surprise attack and routed them.

sentences.zh: 以功遷大將軍，封晉昌縣伯；

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Grand General and enfeoffed as Earl of Jinchang County;
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he was made grand general and enfeoffed as Earl of Jinchang;

sentences.zh: 拜其父壽為少府監，聽不事。

translations.literal: his father Shou was appointed Director of the Palace Workshops, with permission not to serve.
translations.idiomatic: his father Shou was appointed director of the Palace Workshops with permission to hold the title without serving.

sentences.zh: 君㚟凱旋，玄宗宴君㚟及妻夏於廣達樓，賜金帛，夏亦自以戰功封武威郡夫人。

translations.literal: When Jun'ou returned in triumph Xuanzong feasted Jun'ou and his wife Xia at the Guangda Tower and bestowed gold and silk; Xia too was enfeoffed as Lady of Wuwei Commandery for her own merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: On his triumphant return Xuanzong entertained Jun'ou and his wife Xia at the Guangda Tower with gifts of gold and silk; Xia was also enfeoffed as Lady of Wuwei for her own battlefield achievements.

sentences.zh: 俄而吐蕃陷瓜州，執刺史田元獻及壽，殺居人，取資糧，進攻玉門軍，使人靳君㚟曰：「將軍常自以忠勇，今不一進戰，奈何？」

translations.literal: Before long Tibet took Guazhou, seized Governor Tian Yuanxian and Shou, killed the inhabitants, took supplies, and advanced against Yumen Army; they sent someone to mock Jun'ou, saying: "The general always considers himself loyal and brave—why will he not advance to battle now?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tibet captured Guazhou, took Governor Tian Yuanxian and Shou prisoner, slaughtered the inhabitants, seized supplies, and marched on Yumen Army; they sent a messenger to taunt Jun'ou: "You always boast of loyalty and courage—why won't you come out and fight?"

sentences.zh: 君㚟登陴西向哭，兵不敢出。

translations.literal: Jun'ou mounted the ramparts and wept facing west; his troops dared not sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the wall and wept toward the west, and his soldiers did not dare march out.

sentences.zh: 初，涼州有回紇、契、思結、渾四部，世為酋長，君㚟微時，數往來，為所輕。

translations.literal: Earlier in Liangzhou there were four tribal groups—Uyghur, Qi, Sinijie, and Hun—who for generations had been chieftains; when Jun'ou was still obscure he often came and went among them and was looked down upon.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou had long been home to four tribal groups—the Uyghurs, Qi, Sinijie, and Hun—whose families had served as chieftains for generations; in his early days Jun'ou moved among them often and was held in contempt.

sentences.zh: 及節度河西，回紇等頗鞅鞅，恥為下。

translations.literal: When he became military commissioner of Hexi the Uyghurs and others were quite discontented, ashamed to be subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became military commissioner of Hexi, the Uyghurs and the others were resentful and ashamed to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 君㚟怒，數督過之。

translations.literal: Jun'ou grew angry and repeatedly censured their faults.
translations.idiomatic: Jun'ou grew angry and repeatedly rebuked them for their faults.

sentences.zh: 既怨望，潛遣人至東都言狀。

translations.literal: Once resentful, they secretly sent men to the eastern capital to report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Filled with resentment, they secretly sent envoys to the eastern capital to lodge complaints.

sentences.zh: 君㚟間驛奏四部有叛謀，帝使中人即訊，回紇不能自直。

translations.literal: Jun'ou intercepted the relay post and memorialized that the four groups were plotting rebellion; the emperor sent eunuchs to investigate on the spot, and the Uyghurs could not clear themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Jun'ou intercepted their dispatches and reported that the four groups were plotting rebellion; the emperor sent eunuchs to investigate immediately, and the Uyghurs could not vindicate themselves.

sentences.zh: 於是瀚海大都督回紇承宗流州，渾大得流吉州，賀蘭都督契承明流藤州，盧山都督思結歸國流瓊州，而承宗黨瀚海州司馬護輸等益不平，思有以復怨。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengzong, Grand Commander of Hanhai and Uyghur, was exiled to Liuzhou; Dadé of the Hun to Jizhou; Chengming, Governor of Helan of the Qi, to Tengzhou; Guiguo, Governor of Lushan of the Sinijie, to Qiongzhou; while Chengzong's partisans such as Huyu, military administrator of Hanhai Prefecture, grew still more resentful and thought how to repay the grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong, Uyghur grand commander of Hanhai, was exiled to Liuzhou; Dadé of the Hun to Jizhou; Chengming, Qi governor of Helan, to Tengzhou; and Guiguo, Sinijie governor of Lushan, to Qiongzhou. Chengzong's followers, including Huyu, military administrator of Hanhai, grew still angrier and plotted revenge.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃使間道走突厥，君㚟率騎到肅州掩取之，還至甘州，護輸狙兵發，奪君㚟節，殺左右親吏，剖其心，曰：「是始謀者。」

translations.literal: It happened that a Tibetan envoy was traveling by a secret route toward the Turks; Jun'ou led cavalry to Suzhou and seized him; on the return to Ganzhou, Huyu lay in ambush and sprang up, seized Jun'ou's command tally, killed his close attendants, cut out his heart, and said: "This was the original plotter."
translations.idiomatic: When a Tibetan envoy was slipping through by a hidden route toward the Turks, Jun'ou led horsemen to Suzhou and captured him. On the way back to Ganzhou, Huyu sprang an ambush, seized Jun'ou's command tally, killed his personal staff, cut out his heart, and cried, "This was the man who plotted it all."

sentences.zh: 君㚟引帳下力戰，兵盡乃死。

translations.literal: Jun'ou led his personal guard in fierce fighting and died only when his troops were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Jun'ou led his household guard in a last stand and fell only when his men were spent.

sentences.zh: 輸欲以屍奔吐蕃，追兵至，乃棄屍去。

translations.literal: Huyu wished to carry the corpse to Tibet, but pursuing troops arrived and he abandoned the body and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Huyu tried to carry the body to the Tibetans, but pursuers caught up and he abandoned the corpse and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝痛惜之，贈特進、荊州大都督。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved for him and posthumously granted him Special Advancement and the post of Grand Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply and posthumously made him Special Advancement and grand governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以喪還京師，官護其葬。

translations.literal: His coffin was returned to the capital, and officials escorted the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: His body was brought back to the capital with an official funeral escort.

sentences.zh: 詔張說刻文墓碑，帝自書以寵之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhang Yue to inscribe the tomb stele text, and the emperor himself wrote it as a mark of favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue was ordered to compose the tomb inscription, and the emperor wrote it in his own hand as a special honor.

sentences.zh: 始，吐蕃寇瓜州，分遣莽布支攻常樂，令賈師順乘城守。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tibet raided Guazhou, they separately sent Mangbuzhi to attack Changle and ordered Jia Shishun to mount the walls and defend.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet first raided Guazhou, they sent Mangbuzhi against Changle while Jia Shishun was ordered to hold the city walls.

sentences.zh: 俄而瓜州陷，悉諾邏並兵攻之。

translations.literal: Before long Guazhou fell, and Sinuoluo combined his forces to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guazhou fell, and Sinuoluo joined his forces to besiege Changle.

sentences.zh: 數日，虜眾有姻家在城中，使夜見師順曰：「州已失守，虜悉眾來，孤城渠可久，不早降以全噍類乎？」

translations.literal: After several days, among the enemy host were in-laws within the city; they sent someone by night to see Shishun and say: "The prefecture is already lost, the enemy are coming with their full strength—how long can a lone city hold out? Will you not surrender early to preserve your kind?"
translations.idiomatic: After several days, enemy soldiers with kin inside the city sent a messenger by night to Shishun: "The prefecture is lost and the full enemy host is coming—how long can one isolated city last? Surrender now and save your people."

sentences.zh: 師順曰：「吾受天子命守此，義不可下賊。」

translations.literal: Shishun said: "I have received the Son of Heaven's command to hold this place; by duty I cannot submit to the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Shishun replied, "The Son of Heaven charged me to hold this place; I cannot in honor surrender to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 數日，又說師順曰：「明府不降，吾眾且還，宜有以贈我。」

translations.literal: After several more days they again urged Shishun: "If the prefect will not surrender, our host is about to withdraw—you should have something to give us."
translations.idiomatic: A few days later they pressed him again: "If you will not surrender, we are leaving soon—you should give us something."

sentences.zh: 師順請脫士卒衣襦。

translations.literal: Shishun asked that the soldiers remove their jackets and short coats.
translations.idiomatic: Shishun had the soldiers strip off their jackets and give them up.

sentences.zh: 悉諾邏知無有，乃夜徹營去，毀瓜州城。

translations.literal: Sinuoluo, seeing there was nothing more to gain, withdrew his camp by night and destroyed the walls of Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing nothing more to be had, Sinuoluo broke camp by night, withdrew, and demolished the walls of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 師順開門收器械，復完守備。

translations.literal: Shishun opened the gates, gathered weapons, and restored the defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Shishun opened the gates, collected the abandoned arms, and restored the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃果使精騎還襲，見有備，乃去。

translations.literal: Tibet indeed sent elite cavalry back in a surprise attack; seeing preparations in place, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans did send elite horsemen back in a raid, but finding the city ready, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以功遷鄯州都督、隴右節度使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Governor of Shanzhou and military commissioner of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made governor of Shanzhou and military commissioner of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 師順，岐州人，終左領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Shishun was a man of Qizhou and ended as General of the Left Leading Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shishun, a native of Qizhou, ended his career as general of the Left Leading Army.

sentences.zh: 張守珪

translations.literal: = Zhang Shougui =
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui

sentences.zh: 張守珪，陜州河北人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shougui was a man of Hebei in Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui came from Hebei in Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 姿幹瑰壯，慷慨尚節義，善騎射。

translations.literal: His bearing was magnificent and robust; he was bold-spirited and valued integrity, and skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Imposing in stature, he was ardent, devoted to honor, and expert in riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 以平樂府別將從郭虔瓘守北庭。

translations.literal: As deputy commander of Pingle Prefecture he followed Guo Qianzhen in defending Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: As deputy commander of Pingle he served under Guo Qianzhen at Beiting.

sentences.zh: 突厥侵輪臺，遣守珪往援，中道逢賊，苦戰，斬首千餘級，禽頡斤一人。

translations.literal: When the Turks invaded Luntai he was sent to aid; on the road he met the enemy, fought bitterly, cut off more than a thousand heads, and captured one irkin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks attacked Luntai he was sent to relieve it, met the enemy on the march, fought hard, took more than a thousand heads, and captured an irkin.

sentences.zh: 開元初，虜復攻北庭，守珪從儳道奏事京師，因上書言利害，請引兵出蒲昌、輪臺夾擊賊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan the enemy again attacked Beiting; Shougui was returning to the capital by a side route to report affairs and submitted a memorial on strategy, asking to lead troops out from Puchang and Luntai in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan the enemy attacked Beiting again; Shougui was traveling to the capital by a side road and memorialized on strategy, proposing a pincer from Puchang and Luntai.

sentences.zh: 再遷幽州良杜府果毅。

translations.literal: He was twice transferred to garrison commander of Liangdu Prefecture in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose twice to garrison commander of Liangdu in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 時盧齊卿為刺史，器之，引與共榻坐，謂曰：「不十年，子當節度是州，為國重將，願以子孫托，可僚屬相期邪？」

translations.literal: At the time Lu Qiqing was prefect and valued him, drawing him to sit on the same couch and saying: "Within ten years you will command this prefecture as military commissioner and become a great general of the state; I wish to entrust my descendants to you—may we look to each other as colleagues?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qiqing, then prefect, took a liking to him, had him sit on the same couch, and said, "Within ten years you will command this region as military commissioner and become one of the empire's great generals; may I entrust my family to you as a colleague?"

sentences.zh: 稍遷建康軍使。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to commander of the Jiankang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of the Jiankang army.

sentences.zh: 王君㚟死，河西震懼，詔以守珪為瓜州刺史、墨離軍使，督餘眾完故城。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun'ou died the Hexi region was shaken with fear; an edict made Shougui Governor of Guazhou and commander of the Moli Army, supervising the remaining troops in restoring the old city.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Jun'ou's death the Hexi frontier was terrified; Shougui was made governor of Guazhou and commander of the Moli army to rebuild the old city with the survivors.

sentences.zh: 版築方立，虜奄至，眾失色。

translations.literal: The ramparts were just being raised when the enemy suddenly arrived and the troops turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: The walls were barely rising when the enemy appeared without warning and the men lost their color.

sentences.zh: 守珪曰：「創痍之餘，詎可矢石相確，須權以勝之。」

translations.literal: Shougui said: "In our battered state, how can we meet them with arrows and stones? We must use stratagem to overcome them."
translations.idiomatic: Shougui said, "We are still recovering from wounds—how can we meet them head on with arrows and stones? We must outwit them."

sentences.zh: 遂置酒城上，會諸將作樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set out wine on the walls and gathered the generals for music.
translations.idiomatic: He had wine set out on the walls and entertained his generals with music.

sentences.zh: 虜疑有備，不敢攻，引去，守珪縱兵擊敗之。

translations.literal: The enemy suspected preparations and dared not attack, withdrew, and Shougui sent his troops in pursuit and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy suspected a trap, refused to attack, and withdrew; Shougui then sallied forth and routed them.

sentences.zh: 於是修復位署，招流冗使復業。

translations.literal: Thereupon he restored offices and posts and summoned displaced people to return to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He then restored government offices and brought displaced people back to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 有詔以瓜州為都督府，即詔守珪為都督。

translations.literal: An edict made Guazhou a protectorate prefecture, and immediately appointed Shougui protector.
translations.idiomatic: Guazhou was made a protectorate, and Shougui was appointed its protector.

sentences.zh: 州地沙塉不可蓺，常瀦雪水溉田。

translations.literal: The prefecture's land was sandy and barren and could not be planted; they usually dammed meltwater to irrigate the fields.
translations.idiomatic: The region was sandy and unfit for farming; fields were watered by damming snowmelt.

sentences.zh: 是時，渠堨為虜毀，材木無所出。

translations.literal: At that time the canals and dikes had been destroyed by the enemy and there was no timber to be had.
translations.idiomatic: The canals and dikes had been destroyed by the enemy, and timber was nowhere to be found.

sentences.zh: 守珪密禱於神，一昔水暴至，大木數千章塞流下，因取之，修復堰防，耕者如舊，州人神之，刻石紀事。

translations.literal: Shougui secretly prayed to the spirits; in one night floodwaters suddenly rose and thousands of great logs choked the current downstream; he took them, restored the dikes, and farmers worked as before; the people of the prefecture regarded it as divine and carved stone to record the event.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui prayed in secret; overnight a flood brought thousands of logs downstream. He used them to rebuild the dikes, farming resumed as before, and the people carved a stone to commemorate the miracle.

sentences.zh: 遷鄯州刺史、隴右節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Shanzhou and military commissioner of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Shanzhou and military commissioner of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 徙幽州長史、河北節度副大使。

translations.literal: He was moved to Chief Administrator of Youzhou and deputy military commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief administrator of Youzhou and deputy military commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 俄加采訪處置等使。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made investigation and disposition commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made investigation and disposition commissioner.

sentences.zh: 契丹、奚連年梗邊，牙官可突於，胡有謀者，前長史趙含章、薛楚玉等不能制，守珪至，每戰輒勝，虜遂大敗。

translations.literal: The Khitan and Xi had for years obstructed the border; the military officer Ketuyu, a man of schemes among the barbarians, had not been controlled by former chief administrators Zhao Hanzhang, Xue Chuyu, and others; when Shougui arrived he won every battle and the enemy suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: For years the Khitan and Xi had harassed the frontier; Ketuyu, a cunning tribal officer, had defied earlier administrators Zhao Hanzhang and Xue Chuyu, but once Shougui arrived he won every battle and the tribes were routed.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，詔有司告九廟。

translations.literal: The emperor rejoiced and ordered the authorities to report to the Nine Temples.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejoiced and ordered the victory reported to the imperial ancestors.

sentences.zh: 契丹酋屈剌及突於恐懼，乃遣使詐降。

translations.literal: The Khitan chieftains Quli and Ketuyu, in fear, then sent envoys in feigned surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan leaders Quli and Ketuyu, terrified, sent envoys offering a false surrender.

sentences.zh: 守珪得其情，遣右衛騎曹王悔詣部計事，屈刺無降意，徙帳稍西北，密引突厥眾將殺悔以叛。

translations.literal: Shougui learned their true intent and sent Wang Hui of the Right Guard Cavalry Bureau to their camp to discuss affairs; Quli had no intent to surrender, shifted his tents slightly northwest, and secretly brought Türk forces to kill Hui and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui saw through them and sent Wang Hui of the Right Guard to negotiate; Quli had no intention of surrendering, shifted camp northwest, and secretly brought in Türks to kill Hui and rebel.

sentences.zh: 契丹別帥李過折與突於爭權不葉，悔因間誘之，夜斬屈剌及突於，盡滅其黨，以眾降。

translations.literal: The Khitan sub-chieftain Li Guozhe was at odds with Ketuyu over power; Hui exploited the rift to entice him, and in the night he cut down Quli and Ketuyu, exterminated their faction, and surrendered with the host.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sub-chief Li Guozhe was locked in a power struggle with Ketuyu; Hui turned him, and in the night Li killed Quli and Ketuyu, destroyed their faction, and surrendered with his followers.

sentences.zh: 守珪次紫蒙川，大閱軍實，賞將士，傳屈刺、突於首於東都。

translations.literal: Shougui halted at Zimeng River, held a great review of military stores, rewarded officers and soldiers, and sent the heads of Quli and Ketuyu to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui encamped at the Zimeng River, reviewed the army's stores, rewarded the troops, and sent Quli's and Ketuyu's heads to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，入見天子，會藉田畢，即酺燕為守珪飲至，帝賦詩寵之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he came to audience with the Son of Heaven; when the plowing ceremony was finished, a feast was held and toasts carried to Shougui; the emperor composed a poem to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he came to court; after the plowing rite the emperor held a feast in his honor and composed a poem to celebrate him.

sentences.zh: 加拜輔國大將軍、右羽林大將軍，賜金彩，授二子官，詔立碑紀功。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Supporting-the-State Grand General and Grand General of the Right Yulin Army, granted gold and brocade, two sons were given offices, and an edict ordered a stele erected to record his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Supporting-the-State Grand General and grand general of the Right Yulin Army, given gold and brocade, two sons received offices, and a victory stele was ordered.

sentences.zh: 久之，復討契丹餘黨於捺祿山，鹵獲不訾。

translations.literal: After a long while he again campaigned against Khitan remnants at Nalushan and took booty beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Later he campaigned again against Khitan remnants at Nalushan and took incalculable booty.

sentences.zh: 會裨將趙堪、白真陀羅等強使平盧軍使烏知義度湟水邀叛奚，且蹂其稼，知義辭不往，真陀羅矯詔脅之。

translations.literal: It happened that subordinate generals Zhao Kan, Bai Zhentuoluo, and others forced the Pinglu army commander Wu Zhiyi to cross the Huangshui to intercept rebellious Xi and trample their crops; Zhiyi declined to go, and Zhentuoluo used a forged edict to threaten him.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate generals Zhao Kan and Bai Zhentuoluo forced the Pinglu commander Wu Zhiyi to cross the Huang River against rebel Xi and trample their crops; Zhiyi refused, and Zhentuoluo threatened him with a forged edict.

sentences.zh: 知義與虜鬥，不勝，還，守珪匿其敗，但上克獲狀。

translations.literal: Zhiyi fought the enemy and was defeated; on his return Shougui concealed the defeat and reported only a victory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi fought and lost; Shougui hid the defeat and reported only success.

sentences.zh: 事頗泄，帝遣謁者牛仙童按實，守珪逼真陀羅自殺，厚賂使者，還奏如狀。

translations.literal: The matter leaked somewhat; the emperor sent the attendant Niu Xiantong to investigate; Shougui forced Zhentuoluo to kill himself, bribed the envoy heavily, and he returned reporting as Shougui had claimed.
translations.idiomatic: Word leaked out; the emperor sent Niu Xiantong to investigate. Shougui drove Zhentuoluo to suicide, bribed the envoy, and received a report confirming his version.

sentences.zh: 後仙童以贓敗，事逮守珪，以功貶括州刺史，疽發背死。

translations.literal: Later Xiantong was ruined for bribery and the affair reached Shougui; because of his past merit he was demoted to Prefect of Kuozhou and died of a carbuncle on his back.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiantong later fell in a bribery scandal the case reached Shougui; he was demoted to prefect of Kuozhou for his earlier service and died of a carbuncle on his back.

sentences.zh: 守珪子 獻誠子獻誠。

translations.literal: Shougui's son Xiancheng—Xiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui's son Xiancheng.

sentences.zh: 獻誠，天寶末，陷安祿山，授偽署。

translations.literal: Xiancheng, at the end of Tianbao, fell into An Lushan's hands and was given a false appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao, Xiancheng was captured by An Lushan and given a post in the rebel administration.

sentences.zh: 後事史思明，將兵數萬守汴州。

translations.literal: Later he served Shi Siming, commanding tens of thousands of troops to hold Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Shi Siming, commanding tens of thousands of men at Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 東都平，史朝義走還汴，獻誠不內，籍所統兵以州降，詔即拜汴州刺史，封南陽郡公。

translations.literal: When the eastern capital was pacified Shi Chaoyi fled back to Bian; Xiancheng would not admit him, registered the troops under his command, and surrendered the prefecture; an edict immediately appointed him Governor of Bianzhou and enfeoffed him as Duke of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern capital was recovered, Shi Chaoyi fled to Bian, but Xiancheng refused him entry, surrendered the city with his army, and was made governor of Bianzhou and Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 改寶應軍左廂兵馬使，更封鄧國公。

translations.literal: He was changed to commander of the left wing of the Baoying Army and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the left wing of the Baoying army and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 既來朝，代宗禮賜尤渥。

translations.literal: When he came to court Emperor Daizong treated and rewarded him with exceptional generosity.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court, Emperor Daizong honored him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 擢山南西道節度使，討南山劇賊高玉，禽之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit and campaigned against the fierce bandit Gao Yu of the southern mountains, capturing him.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of Shannan West and captured the outlaw Gao Yu of the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 俄兼劍南東川節度。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made military commissioner of Jiannan East River Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also held the Jiannan East River command.

sentences.zh: 時崔旰殺郭英乂，獻誠率眾戰梓州，大敗。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Gan killed Guo Yingyi; Xiancheng led his host to battle at Zizhou and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Gan killed Guo Yingyi, Xiancheng marched on Zizhou and was badly beaten.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，以疾歸京師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali he returned to the capital on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 3 he returned to the capital because of illness.

sentences.zh: 舉其弟獻恭自代。

translations.literal: He recommended his younger brother Xiangong to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended his younger brother Xiangong as his successor.

sentences.zh: 以檢校戶部尚書知省事，病甚，固乞辭位，卒。

translations.literal: He was made Acting Minister of Revenue with charge of court affairs; gravely ill, he firmly begged to resign his post and died.
translations.idiomatic: Made acting minister of revenue in charge of court affairs, he grew gravely ill, begged to resign, and died.

sentences.zh: 始，獻誠喜功名，為政寬裕，有機略，隨方制變，而簡廉不逮於父。

translations.literal: From the first Xiancheng delighted in fame and achievement; his government was lenient, he had stratagems and adapted measures to circumstances, yet in simplicity and integrity he did not equal his father.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng loved glory and achievement, governed generously, was resourceful and adaptable, but in simplicity and integrity he fell short of his father.

sentences.zh: 獻誠從弟 獻恭從弟獻恭，數有軍功，以右羽林軍代為節度使。

translations.literal: Xiancheng's younger cousin Xiangong—Xiangong, who had repeated military achievements, replaced him as military commissioner through the Right Yulin Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng's cousin Xiangong, a man of repeated military merit, succeeded him through the Right Yulin Army.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，破吐蕃於岷州。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali he defeated Tibet at Minzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dali era he defeated the Tibetans at Minzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜東都留守，累遷檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Defender of the Eastern Capital and rose through repeated promotions to Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In time he became defender of the eastern capital and rose to acting minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 德宗欲徙盧杞為饒州刺史，給事中袁高上還詔書，苦爭。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong wished to transfer Lu Qi to be Prefect of Raozhou; the Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Gao returned the edict and argued bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong tried to transfer Lu Qi to prefect of Raozhou, Attendant Yuan Gao returned the edict and argued fiercely against it.

sentences.zh: 獻恭見帝曰：「高所奏宜聽。」

translations.literal: Xiangong saw the emperor and said: "What Gao has memorialized should be heeded."
translations.idiomatic: Xiangong told the emperor, "Your Majesty should heed what Gao has said."

sentences.zh: 帝不答。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made no answer.

sentences.zh: 復前曰：「高乃陛下良臣，當優異之。」

translations.literal: He stepped forward again and said: "Gao is Your Majesty's worthy minister and should be treated with special favor."
translations.idiomatic: He stepped forward again: "Gao is a worthy minister of yours and deserves special favor."

sentences.zh: 上遂不徙杞。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon did not transfer Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then abandoned the transfer of Lu Qi.

sentences.zh: 世咨其不橈。

translations.literal: The age praised him for not bending.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised him for standing firm.

sentences.zh: 獻恭子 煦子煦，積閥亦至夏州節度使。

translations.literal: Xiangong's son Xu—Xu, who through accumulated merit also rose to military commissioner of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangong's son Xu rose through merit to military commissioner of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 元和八年，振武軍逐節度使李進賢，屠其家及判官嚴澈。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe the Zhenwu Army drove out military commissioner Li Jinxian and slaughtered his family and the judge Yan Che.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 8 the Zhenwu army expelled Commissioner Li Jinxian and massacred his family and judge Yan Che.

sentences.zh: 憲宗怒，詔煦以本軍進討，許以便宜，賜縑三萬為軍資，河東王鍔遣兵五千為援。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was enraged and ordered Xu to advance with his own army to punish them, granting discretionary authority, bestowing thirty thousand bolts of silk as military funds, and Wang E of Hedong sent five thousand troops as reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong ordered Xu to march with his army, granted him full discretion, gave thirty thousand bolts of silk for supplies, and Wang E of Hedong sent five thousand reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 煦入，捕亂卒蘇國珍等數百人，誅之。

translations.literal: Xu entered, seized the mutinous soldiers Su Guozhen and several hundred others, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Xu entered, seized Su Guozhen and several hundred mutineers, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 獻誠從弟 獻甫獻誠從弟獻甫，以軍功試光祿卿、殿中監，從河中節度使賈耽討梁崇義有勞。

translations.literal: Xiancheng's younger cousin Xianfu—Xianfu, who through military merit was tried out as Minister of Imperial Entertainments and Palace Director, followed Hedong military commissioner Jia Dan in campaigning against Liang Chongyi with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng's cousin Xianfu, honored for military service with trial posts as minister of imperial entertainments and palace director, served under Jia Dan of Hedong against Liang Chongyi with distinction.

sentences.zh: 德宗西幸，又從渾瑊討朱泚，戰多，累遷至金吾將軍、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Dezong went west on campaign he again followed Hun Jian against Zhu Ci, fought in many battles, and rose through repeated promotions to General of the Golden Guards and Acting Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong fled west, he followed Hun Jian against Zhu Ci, fought in many battles, and rose to general of the Golden Guards and acting minister of public works.

sentences.zh: 李懷光叛，吐蕃盜邊，獻甫領禁兵戍咸陽累年，兵農悅安。

translations.literal: When Li Huiguang rebelled and Tibet raided the borders, Xianfu led palace troops garrisoned at Xianyang for years; soldiers and farmers were content and secure.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huiguang rebelled and Tibet raided the frontier, Xianfu garrisoned the palace troops at Xianyang for years until soldiers and farmers alike were secure.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，代韓遊瑰領邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan he replaced Han Yougui as military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 4 he replaced Han Yougui as military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 邠寧軍素驕，憚獻甫嚴，因遊瑰去，遂縱掠，邀範希朝為帥。

translations.literal: The Binning army had always been arrogant; they feared Xianfu's severity, and when Yougui departed they plundered freely and invited Fan Xichao to be their commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Binning army was notoriously unruly; they feared Xianfu's strictness, and when Yougui left they looted freely and tried to make Fan Xichao their commander.

sentences.zh: 都將楊朝晟誅首亂者，獻甫乃得入。

translations.literal: The commandant Yang Chaocheng executed the ringleaders of the disorder, and only then could Xianfu enter.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Yang Chaocheng executed the ringleaders, and only then could Xianfu take command.

sentences.zh: 於是斷山浚塹，選巖要地築烽堡。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cut through mountains, deepened ditches, and chose strategic heights to build beacon towers and forts.
translations.idiomatic: He then cut passes through the mountains, dug deep trenches, and built beacon towers and forts on commanding ground.

sentences.zh: 請復鹽州及洪門、洛原鎮屯兵，詔可。

translations.literal: He requested restoring garrisons at Yanzhou and the Hongmen and Luoyuan frontier posts; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to restore garrisons at Yanzhou and the Hongmen and Luoyuan posts, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 獻甫遣兵馬使魏茪逐吐蕃，築鹽、夏二城，虜眾畏，不敢入寇。

translations.literal: Xianfu sent cavalry commander Wei Guang to drive off Tibet, built the cities of Yan and Xia, and the enemy host feared him and dared not raid.
translations.idiomatic: He sent cavalry commander Wei Guang against the Tibetans, built the cities of Yan and Xia, and the enemy dared not raid again.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was additionally made Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 王忠嗣

translations.literal: = Wang Zhongsi =
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongsi

sentences.zh: 王忠嗣，華州鄭人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongsi was a man of Zheng in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongsi was a native of Zheng in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 父海賓，太子右衛率、豐安軍使。

translations.literal: His father Haibin was Commander of the Right Guard of the Heir Apparent and commander of the Feng'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Haibin was commander of the Right Guard of the Heir Apparent and commander of the Feng'an army.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，吐蕃寇隴右，詔隴右防禦使薛訥率杜賓客、郭知運、王晙、安思順禦之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan Tibet raided Longyou; an edict ordered Longyou defense commissioner Xue Ne to lead Du Binke, Guo Zhiyun, Wang Jun, and An Sishun to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 2 Tibet raided Longyou; Xue Ne was ordered to lead Du Binke, Guo Zhiyun, Wang Jun, and An Sishun against them.

sentences.zh: 以海賓為先鋒，戰武階，追北至壕口，殺其眾。

translations.literal: Haibin was made vanguard; they fought at Wujie, pursued north to Haokou, and killed the enemy host.
translations.idiomatic: Haibin led the vanguard, fought at Wujie, pursued the enemy north to Haokou, and killed many.

sentences.zh: 進戰長城堡，諸將冒其功，按兵顧望，海賓戰死，大軍乘之，斬賊萬七千級，獲馬七萬、牛羊四十萬。

translations.literal: Advancing to battle at Changcheng Fort, the generals coveted his merit, held their troops and looked on; Haibin died in battle, the main army pressed the advantage, cut off seventeen thousand enemy heads, and seized seventy thousand horses and four hundred thousand cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: At Changcheng Fort the other generals held back to claim his glory while Haibin fought and died; the main army then pressed forward, killed seventeen thousand of the enemy, and captured seventy thousand horses and four hundred thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 玄宗憐其忠，贈左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: Xuanzong pitied his loyalty and posthumously made him Grand General of the Left Golden Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong mourned his loyalty and posthumously made him grand general of the Left Golden Guards.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣時年九歲，始名訓，授尚輦奉御。

translations.literal: Zhongsi was then nine years old; his original name was Xun, and he was appointed Palanquin Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi was then nine; originally named Xun, he was appointed palanquin attendant.

sentences.zh: 入見帝，伏地號泣，帝撫之曰：「此去病孤也，須壯而將之。」

translations.literal: On entering to see the emperor he prostrated himself wailing; the emperor comforted him and said: "This is the orphan of Qubing; when he is grown I shall make him a general."
translations.idiomatic: When he was brought before the emperor he prostrated himself and wept; the emperor comforted him and said, "This is the orphan of Huo Qubing; when he is grown I shall make him a general."

sentences.zh: 更賜今名，養禁中。

translations.literal: He was given his present name and raised within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was given his present name and raised in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 肅宗為忠王，帝使與遊。

translations.literal: When Suzong was Prince of Zhong the emperor had them play together.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong was Prince of Zhong, the emperor had the two boys play together.

sentences.zh: 及長，雄毅寡言，有武略，上與論兵，應對蜂起，帝器之，曰：「後日爾為良將。」

translations.literal: When he had grown up he was bold and resolute, sparing of speech, and possessed military stratagems; the emperor discussed warfare with him and his replies came in swarms; the emperor valued him and said: "In days to come you will be a fine general."
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he was bold, reserved, and skilled in military affairs; when the emperor discussed strategy with him his answers came in a flood, and the emperor said, "One day you will be a fine general."

sentences.zh: 試守代州別駕，大猾閉門自斂，不敢幹法。

translations.literal: He was tried out as acting Governor of Daizhou; great ruffians shut their doors and restrained themselves, not daring to violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting governor of Daizhou; local bullies shut themselves in and dared not break the law.

sentences.zh: 數以輕騎出塞，忠王言於帝曰：「忠嗣敢鬥，恐亡之。」

translations.literal: He often led light cavalry beyond the frontier; the Prince of Zhong told the emperor: "Zhongsi is bold in fighting—I fear we may lose him."
translations.idiomatic: He often led light cavalry beyond the border; the Prince of Zhong told the emperor, "Zhongsi is so eager to fight that I fear we may lose him."

sentences.zh: 由是召還。

translations.literal: On this account he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled for that reason.

sentences.zh: 信安王祎在河東，蕭嵩出河西，數引為麾下。

translations.literal: When Prince Xin'an Yi was in Hedong and Xiao Song went out to Hexi, they repeatedly took him into their staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Prince Xin'an Yi in Hedong and Xiao Song in Hexi, he was repeatedly taken onto their staffs.

sentences.zh: 帝以其年少，有復讎誌，詔不得特將。

translations.literal: Because he was still young and bore a desire for revenge, an edict forbade him to command armies independently.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was young and burning for revenge, the emperor forbade him independent command.

sentences.zh: 嵩入朝，忠嗣曰：「從公三年，無以歸報天子。」

translations.literal: When Song entered court Zhongsi said: "I have followed you for three years with nothing to bring back in repayment to the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When Song went to court, Zhongsi said, "I have served you three years with nothing to show the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 乃請精銳數百襲虜。

translations.literal: He then asked for several hundred elite troops to raid the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for several hundred picked men to raid the enemy.

sentences.zh: 會贊普大酋閱武郁標川，其下欲還，忠嗣不從，提刀略陣，斬數千人，獲羊馬萬計。

translations.literal: It happened that the qaghan's great chieftains were reviewing troops at Yubiao River; his followers wished to return, but Zhongsi would not agree; he seized his blade and swept the line, cutting down several thousand men and seizing tens of thousands of sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan's great chiefs were reviewing troops at the Yubiao River; when they wanted to withdraw Zhongsi refused, charged the line with drawn sword, killed several thousand, and captured tens of thousands of sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 嵩上其功，帝大悅。

translations.literal: Song reported his merit and the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Song reported the victory and the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 累遷左威衛將軍、代北都督，封清源縣男。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became General of the Left Weiwu Guard and Governor of Daibei, enfeoffed as Baron of Qingyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general of the Left Weiwu Guard and governor of Daibei, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 與皇甫惟明輕重不得，構忠嗣罪，貶東陽府左果毅。

translations.literal: He and Huangfu Weiming could not agree on precedence; Weiming fabricated charges against Zhongsi and he was demoted to left garrison commander of Dongyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with Huangfu Weiming over precedence; Weiming framed him and he was demoted to left garrison commander of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使杜希望欲取吐蕃新羅城，有言忠嗣才者，希望以聞，詔追赴河西，進拔其城。

translations.literal: Hexi military commissioner Du Xiwang wished to take Tibet's Xinluo City; someone spoke of Zhongsi's talent, Xiwang reported it, and an edict recalled him to Hexi; he advanced and captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Hexi commissioner Du Xiwang planned to take the Tibetan city of Xinluo, Zhongsi's ability was recommended, he was recalled to Hexi, and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣錄多，授左威衛郎將，專知兵馬。

translations.literal: Zhongsi's record of merit was great; he was appointed Commandant of the Left Weiwu Guard with sole charge of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: For his many achievements he was made commandant of the Left Weiwu Guard with sole charge of the army.

sentences.zh: 俄吐蕃大出，欲取當新城，晨壓官軍陣，眾不敵，舉軍皆恐。

translations.literal: Before long Tibet came out in force, intending to take Dangxincheng; at dawn they pressed the government army's line; the troops could not match them and the whole army was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Tibetans marched out in force against Dangxincheng, pressed the imperial line at dawn, and the whole army feared defeat.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣單馬進，左右馳突，獨殺數百人，賊眾囂相蹂，軍{廣多}翼掩之，虜大敗。

translations.literal: Zhongsi advanced alone on horseback; his attendants charged to and fro; he himself killed several hundred men; the enemy host clamored and trampled one another; the army's wings closed on them and the barbarians suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi rode forward alone while his men charged about him, killing hundreds himself; the enemy panicked and trampled one another as the army's wings closed in and routed them.

sentences.zh: 拜左金吾衛將軍，領河東節度副使、大同軍使，尋為節度使。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Left Golden Guards, acting Hedong circuit deputy commissioner and commander of the Datong Army, and soon became military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the Left Golden Guards, deputy commissioner of Hedong and commander of the Datong army, and soon full military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，節度朔方，兼靈州都督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was military commissioner of Shuofang and concurrently Governor of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he commanded Shuofang and served concurrently as governor of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，北討奚怒皆，戰桑幹河，三遇三克，耀武漠北，高會而還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he campaigned north against the Xi Nujie, fought on the Sanggan River, met them three times and conquered three times, displayed martial might north of the desert, held a grand feast, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 he campaigned north against the Xi Nujie, fought three victorious battles on the Sanggan River, displayed his power in the northern desert, feasted his army, and returned.

sentences.zh: 時突厥新有難，忠嗣進軍磧口經略之。

translations.literal: At the time the Turks had newly fallen into difficulty; Zhongsi advanced his army to Qikou to conduct frontier operations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks were newly in turmoil, Zhongsi advanced to Qikou to manage the frontier.

sentences.zh: 烏蘇米施可汗請降，忠嗣以其方強，特文降耳，乃營木剌、蘭山，諜虛實。

translations.literal: The qaghan Wusumishi requested surrender; Zhongsi considered their side still strong and that this was only a feigned surrender in writing; he encamped at Mula and Lanshan and spied out their true condition.
translations.idiomatic: When Qaghan Wusumishi offered surrender, Zhongsi judged it a paper submission while the Turks remained strong; he encamped at Mula and Lanshan and sent spies to learn their strength.

sentences.zh: 因上平戎十八策，縱反間於拔悉密與葛邏祿、回紇三部，攻多羅斯城，涉昆水，斬米施可汗，築大同、靜邊二城，徙清塞、橫野軍實之，並受降、振武為一城，自是虜不敢盜塞。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted the Eighteen Stratagems for Pacifying the Barbarians, sowed dissension among the Basmyl, Qarluk, and Uyghur three groups, attacked Duoluosi City, crossed the Kun River, beheaded Qaghan Mishishi, built the two cities of Datong and Jingbian, moved the Qingse and Hengye armies to fill them, and combined Shoujiang and Zhenwu into one city; from this time the barbarians dared not raid the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the Eighteen Stratagems for Pacifying the Barbarians, set the Basmyl, Qarluk, and Uyghurs against one another, took Duoluosi, crossed the Kun River, killed Qaghan Mishishi, built Datong and Jingbian, garrisoned them with the Qingse and Hengye armies, united Shoujiang and Zhenwu into one fortress, and thereafter the nomads dared not raid the border.

sentences.zh: 徙河東節度使，進封縣公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Hedong and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of a county.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of Hedong and promoted to county duke.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣本負勇敢，及為將，乃能持重安邊，不生事，嘗曰：「平世為將，撫眾而已。

translations.literal: Zhongsi had originally relied on courage, but once he became a general he could hold his weight, secure the frontier, and create no incidents; he once said: "In peaceful times a general need only comfort his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Though naturally brave, as a commander he was steady and kept the frontier quiet; he said, "In peacetime a general need only care for his men.

sentences.zh: 吾不欲竭中國力以幸功名。」

translations.literal: I do not wish to exhaust the strength of China to chase after fame and achievement."
translations.idiomatic: I will not drain the empire's strength for my own glory."

sentences.zh: 故訓練士馬，隨缺繕補。

translations.literal: Therefore he trained soldiers and horses and repaired deficiencies as they arose.
translations.idiomatic: He trained men and horses and repaired equipment as needed.

sentences.zh: 有漆弓百五十斤，每弢之，示無所用。

translations.literal: He had a lacquered bow of one hundred fifty jin, which he always kept in its case to show he had no use for it.
translations.idiomatic: He owned a lacquered bow of one hundred fifty jin but always kept it cased to show he had no wish to use it.

sentences.zh: 軍中士氣盛，日夜思戰，忠嗣縱詭間，伺虜隙，時時出奇兵襲敵，所向無不克，故士亦樂為用。

translations.literal: Morale in the army was high and day and night they longed for battle; Zhongsi employed stratagems and spies, watched for enemy openings, and from time to time sent surprise forces to raid the foe; wherever they went they did not fail to conquer, and therefore the troops were also glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Morale ran high and the men burned to fight; Zhongsi used spies and stratagems, struck whenever the enemy slipped, and won every battle, so his troops served him gladly.

sentences.zh: 軍每出，召屬長付以兵，使授士卒，雖弓矢亦誌姓名其上。

translations.literal: Whenever the army went out he summoned unit leaders, entrusted them with weapons, and had them issue them to the soldiers—even on bows and arrows he marked names.
translations.idiomatic: Before each campaign he called unit leaders, issued arms through them to the men, and even marked names on bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 軍還，遣弦亡鏃，皆按名第罪。

translations.literal: When the army returned, for every missing bowstring or arrowhead he punished by name in order.
translations.idiomatic: On return, every missing bowstring or arrowhead was charged to the named soldier.

sentences.zh: 以是部下人自觀，器甲充刃。

translations.literal: Because of this his subordinates watched themselves, and weapons and armor were sharp and full.
translations.idiomatic: His men therefore kept themselves in order, and arms and armor were always complete and sharp.

sentences.zh: 自朔方至雲中袤數千里，據要險築城堡，斥地甚遠。

translations.literal: From Shuofang to Yunzhong for several thousand li he seized strategic points and built forts and castles, extending territory very far.
translations.idiomatic: From Shuofang to Yunzhong he built forts on strategic ground across thousands of li, pushing the frontier far outward.

sentences.zh: 自張仁亶後四十餘年，忠嗣繼其功。

translations.literal: More than forty years after Zhang Renguan, Zhongsi continued his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty years after Zhang Renguan, Zhongsi carried on his work.

sentences.zh: 俄為河西、隴右節度使，權朔方、河東節度，佩四將印，勁兵重地，控制萬里，近世未有也。

translations.literal: Before long he was military commissioner of Hexi and Longyou, acting commissioner of Shuofang and Hedong, bearing four generals' seals, with crack troops in vital regions controlling ten thousand li—nothing like it in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he commanded Hexi and Longyou and acted for Shuofang and Hedong, bearing four generals' seals over crack troops in vital regions across ten thousand li—unprecedented in recent memory.

sentences.zh: 又授一子五品官。

translations.literal: One son was also granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: One of his sons received a fifth-rank post.

sentences.zh: 後數出戰青海、積石，虜輒奔破。

translations.literal: Later he campaigned several times at Qinghai and Jishi; the enemy always fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought repeatedly at Qinghai and Jishi, and the enemy always broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 又討吐谷渾於墨離，平其國。

translations.literal: He also campaigned against the Tuyuhun at Moli and pacified their state.
translations.idiomatic: He also campaigned against the Tuyuhun at Moli and pacified their realm.

sentences.zh: 乃固讓朔方、河東二節度，許之。

translations.literal: He then firmly declined the two commands of Shuofang and Hedong, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He then firmly declined the Shuofang and Hedong commands, and the emperor agreed.
