sentences.zh: 帝方事石堡城，詔問攻取計，忠嗣奏言：「吐蕃舉國守之，若頓兵堅城下，費士數萬，然後可圖，恐所得不讎所失，請厲兵馬，待釁取之。」

translations.literal: The emperor was then bent on Shibao City and ordered inquiry into plans for its capture; Zhongsi memorialized: "Tibet is defending it with the whole state; if we halt our troops beneath a strong wall, we will spend tens of thousands of soldiers before it can be taken—I fear the gain will not repay the loss; I ask to sharpen troops and horses and wait for an opening to seize it."
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor pressed the attack on Shibao City, Zhongsi advised: "Tibet is defending it with the whole kingdom; a siege would cost tens of thousands of lives, and the gain may not repay the loss. Sharpen the army and wait for an opening."

sentences.zh: 帝意不快。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased in mind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 而李林甫尤忌其功，日鉤摭過咎。

translations.literal: Li Linfu especially envied his achievements and daily gathered and collected his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu especially resented his success and daily hunted for faults.

sentences.zh: 會董延光建言請下石堡，詔忠嗣分兵應接，忠嗣不得已為出軍，而士無賞格，延光不悅。

translations.literal: It happened that Dong Yanguang proposed taking Shibao; an edict ordered Zhongsi to divide troops in support; Zhongsi had no choice but to send out the army, yet the soldiers had no scale of rewards, and Yanguang was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Yanguang proposed taking Shibao, Zhongsi was ordered to support him; Zhongsi sent troops reluctantly without offering rewards, and Yanguang was angry.

sentences.zh: 河西兵馬使李光弼入說曰：「大夫愛惜士卒，有拒延光心，雖名受詔，實奪其謀。

translations.literal: Hexi cavalry commander Li Guangbi entered and urged him: "The grandee cherishes his soldiers and has a mind to refuse Yanguang; though in name he accepts the edict, in fact he is thwarting his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi of Hexi urged him: "You are sparing your men and resisting Yanguang; though you obey the edict in name, you are blocking his plan.

sentences.zh: 然大夫已付萬眾，而不立重賞，何以賈士勇？

translations.literal: Yet the grandee has already committed ten thousand men and established no heavy rewards—how can he purchase the soldiers' courage?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have committed ten thousand men without offering great rewards—how will you buy their courage?

sentences.zh: 且大夫惜數萬段賜，以啟讒口，有如不捷，歸罪大夫，大夫先受禍矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, if the grandee spares tens of thousands of bolts in gifts and thereby opens the mouths of slanderers, should there be no success the blame will fall on the grandee and he will suffer first."
translations.idiomatic: If you withhold tens of thousands of bolts in rewards, you invite slander; if the attack fails, the blame will fall on you first."

sentences.zh: 忠嗣曰：「吾固審得一城不足制敵，失之未害於國。

translations.literal: Zhongsi said: "I have long understood that gaining one city is not enough to control the enemy, and losing it would not harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi said, "I know one city will not break the enemy, and losing it would not harm the state.

sentences.zh: 吾忍以數萬人命易一官哉！

translations.literal: How could I bear to trade tens of thousands of lives for one office!
translations.idiomatic: How could I trade tens of thousands of lives for one promotion!

sentences.zh: 明日見責，不失一金吾、羽林將軍，歸宿衛；

translations.literal: If tomorrow I am blamed, I shall lose no more than a post as Golden Guard or Yulin general and return to palace guard duty;
translations.idiomatic: If I am blamed tomorrow, I lose no more than a post as Golden Guard or Yulin general and return to the palace guard;

sentences.zh: 不者，黔中上佐耳。」

translations.literal: otherwise, a senior aide in Qianzhong."
translations.idiomatic: at worst, a senior aide in Qianzhong."

sentences.zh: 光弼謝曰：「大夫乃行古人事，光弼又何言！」

translations.literal: Guangbi apologized and said: "The grandee is acting as the ancients did—what more can Guangbi say!"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi withdrew, saying, "You are acting as the ancients did—what more can I say!"

sentences.zh: 趨而出。

translations.literal: He hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried out.

sentences.zh: 延光過期不克，果訴忠嗣沮兵。

translations.literal: Yanguang passed the deadline without success and indeed accused Zhongsi of obstructing the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang missed his deadline and accused Zhongsi of obstructing the campaign.

sentences.zh: 又安祿山城雄武，扼飛狐塞，謀亂，請忠嗣助役，因欲留其兵；

translations.literal: An Lushan was fortifying Xiongwu, holding Feihu Pass, plotting rebellion, and asked Zhongsi to help with the labor, intending thereby to detain his troops;
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan was fortifying Xiongwu at Feihu Pass and plotting rebellion; he asked Zhongsi to help with the work, hoping to keep his troops;

sentences.zh: 忠嗣先期至，不見祿山而還。

translations.literal: Zhongsi arrived ahead of time, did not see Lushan, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi arrived early, did not meet Lushan, and returned.

sentences.zh: 數上言祿山且亂，林甫益惡之，陰使人誣告「忠嗣嘗養宮中，雲吾欲奉太子」。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized that Lushan was about to rebel; Linfu hated him all the more and secretly sent men to accuse him falsely: "Zhongsi once reared [a child] in the palace, saying 'I wish to support the Heir Apparent.'"
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly warned that Lushan would rebel; Linfu hated him more and secretly accused him of saying in the palace, "I mean to support the heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，召入付三司訊驗，罪應死。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, summoned him in, and handed him to the Three Offices for examination; the crime warranted death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, had him tried by the Three Offices, and the charge carried death.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰方有寵，白上，請以官爵贖忠嗣罪，帝意解，貶漢陽太守。

translations.literal: Geshu Han was then in favor; he told the emperor and asked to redeem Zhongsi's crime with rank and title; the emperor's mind eased and he was demoted to Prefect of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, then in favor, pleaded to redeem Zhongsi with his own rank; the emperor relented and demoted Zhongsi to prefect of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 久之，徙漢東郡，卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Handong Commandery and died at age forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was moved to Handong and died at forty-five.

sentences.zh: 後翰引兵攻石堡，拔之，死亡略盡，如忠嗣言，故當世號為名將。

translations.literal: Later Han led troops to attack Shibao, took it, and deaths were nearly total, just as Zhongsi had said; therefore his age called him a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han took Shibao at the cost of nearly his whole force, just as Zhongsi had warned, and his age hailed him as a famous general.

sentences.zh: 初，在朔方，至互市，輒高償馬直，諸蕃爭來市，故蕃馬浸少，唐軍精。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Shuofang, whenever he came to the frontier markets he always paid high prices for horses; the various tribes competed to come and trade, so barbarian horses gradually grew fewer and Tang armies were elite.
translations.idiomatic: In Shuofang he paid premium prices at the frontier markets, drawing tribes to sell horses until their stock dwindled and Tang cavalry grew superb.

sentences.zh: 及鎮河、隴，又請徙朔方、河東九千騎以實軍。

translations.literal: When he commanded He and Long he also requested transferring nine thousand horsemen from Shuofang and Hedong to fill out his army.
translations.idiomatic: When he commanded He and Long he also asked to transfer nine thousand horsemen from Shuofang and Hedong to strengthen his army.

sentences.zh: 迄天寶末，益滋息。

translations.literal: Down to the end of Tianbao they increased and flourished still more.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Tianbao they had multiplied still further.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，追贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying he was posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 1 he was posthumously made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：以忠嗣之才，戰必破，攻必克，策石堡之得不當所亡，高馬直以空虜資，論祿山亂有萌，可謂深謀矣。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: With Zhongsi's talent, in battle he always broke the enemy and in attack always conquered; he judged that taking Shibao would not be worth what was lost, paid high prices for horses to drain barbarian resources, and discussed the budding of Lushan's rebellion—this may be called deep strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist writes: Given Zhongsi's talent—victory in every battle and conquest in every assault—he judged Shibao not worth its cost, drained tribal horse stocks with high prices, and foresaw Lushan's rebellion: this was true strategic vision.

sentences.zh: 然不能自免於讒，卒死放地。

translations.literal: Yet he could not save himself from slander and ultimately died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not escape slander and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 自古忠賢，工謀於國則拙於身，多矣，可勝咤哉！

translations.literal: From ancient times loyal worthies skilled in planning for the state have been clumsy in preserving themselves—how many such cases there are; can one not sigh in wonder!
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity loyal men skilled for the state have often been helpless for themselves—how many such cases, and how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 牛仙客

translations.literal: = Niu Xianke =
translations.idiomatic: Niu Xianke

sentences.zh: 牛仙客，涇州鶉觚人。

translations.literal: Niu Xianke was a man of Chunquan in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Xianke was a native of Chunquan in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初為縣小史，令傅文靜器之，會為隴右營田使，引與計事，積功遷洮州司馬。

translations.literal: At first he was a minor clerk in the county; Magistrate Fu Wenjing valued him; when he became Longyou agricultural commissioner he drew him into planning affairs, and through accumulated merit he was promoted to Military Administrator of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a county clerk; Magistrate Fu Wenjing favored him, and when Fu became Longyou agricultural commissioner he brought Xianke into planning and promoted him to military administrator of Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使王君㚟召為判官。

translations.literal: Hexi military commissioner Wang Jun'ou summoned him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun'ou, military commissioner of Hexi, made him administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 君㚟死，仙客獨得免。

translations.literal: When Jun'ou died, Xianke alone escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun'ou was killed, Xianke alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 蕭嵩代節度，復委以軍政。

translations.literal: When Xiao Song replaced him as commissioner he again entrusted him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Song succeeded as commissioner he again put Xianke in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 仙客清勤不懈，接士大夫以信。

translations.literal: Xianke was pure, diligent, and untiring, and received scholar-officials with sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke was scrupulous and tireless, and dealt with officials in good faith.

sentences.zh: 及嵩還執政，因薦之。

translations.literal: When Song returned to hold power he recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Song returned to power he recommended him.

sentences.zh: 稍遷太僕少卿，判涼州別駕，知節度留後事，俄為節度使。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Vice Minister of the Stud, acting Governor of Liangzhou, in charge of circuit affairs as regent, and soon became military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the stud, acting governor of Liangzhou, regent of the circuit, and soon full military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開元二十四年，代信安王祎為朔方行軍大總管。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan he replaced Prince Xin'an Yi as Grand Commander on campaign in Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 24 he replaced Prince Xin'an Yi as grand campaign commander in Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 始在河西，嗇事省用，倉庫積鉅萬，器械犀銳。

translations.literal: When he was first in Hexi he was frugal in affairs and sparing in expenditure; storehouses accumulated tens of thousands and weapons were keen and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: In Hexi he was frugal, amassed vast stores, and kept weapons sharp.

sentences.zh: 崔希逸代之，即以聞。

translations.literal: When Cui Xiyi replaced him he reported this at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Xiyi replaced him he reported this to court.

sentences.zh: 帝令刑部員外郎張利馳傳覆視，如狀。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhang Lichi, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, to go by relay post and verify on the spot; it was as reported.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zhang Lichi of the Ministry of Justice to verify on the spot; all was as reported.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，將用為尚書，宰相張九齡持不可，乃封隴西郡公，實封戶二百。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and was about to appoint him Minister, but Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling objected that this would not do; he was therefore enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi Commandery with two hundred actual fief households.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make him a minister, but Zhang Jiuling objected; instead he was enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi with two hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 李林甫探知帝旨，稱其材。

translations.literal: Li Linfu probed the emperor's intent and praised his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu sensed the emperor's mind and praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 會九齡罷，故以工部尚書、同中書門下三品，知門下事，遙領河東節度副大使。

translations.literal: When Jiuling was dismissed he was therefore made Minister of Public Works, Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery with Third Rank, in charge of the Palace Secretariat, and remotely acting deputy military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiuling fell he was made minister of public works, fellow of the Secretariat with third rank, head of the Palace Secretariat, and titular deputy commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 為相謹身無它，與時沈浮，唯唯恭願。

translations.literal: As chief minister he was cautious in person and without other aims, drifting with the times in compliant assent.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he was cautious and unassuming, drifted with the times, and assented to everything.

sentences.zh: 前後錫與，緘庋不敢用。

translations.literal: Imperial gifts before and after he sealed away in storage and did not dare use.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed away imperial gifts and would not use them.

sentences.zh: 百司諮決，無所處可，輒曰：「如令式。」

translations.literal: When the hundred offices consulted him for decisions and there was nowhere to place them, he would always say: "As the regulations provide."
translations.idiomatic: When offices asked his judgment he would say only, "As the regulations provide."

sentences.zh: 帝既用仙客，知時議不歸，乘間以問高力士，力士曰：「仙客本胥史，非宰相器。」

translations.literal: The emperor, having employed Xianke, knew that contemporary opinion did not rally to him; seizing an opportunity he asked Gao Lishi, who said: "Xianke was originally a clerk—he is not material for chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing opinion did not favor Xianke, the emperor asked Gao Lishi, who said, "Xianke was only a clerk—not chief-minister timber."

sentences.zh: 帝忿然曰：「朕且用康厓！」

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily: "I shall employ Kang Ya!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "Then I will employ Kang Ya!"

sentences.zh: 蓋恚言也。

translations.literal: This was words spoken in anger.
translations.idiomatic: It was an angry remark.

sentences.zh: 有為厓言者，厓以為實，喜甚。

translations.literal: Someone reported this to Ya; Ya took it as real and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Kang Ya, who believed it and was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 久之，封豳國公，加左相。

translations.literal: After a long while he was enfeoffed as Duke of Bin and additionally made Left Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was enfeoffed as Duke of Bin and made left chief minister.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書右丞相，謚曰貞簡。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Right Chief Minister of the Department of State Affairs, with posthumous title Zhenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made right chief minister, with the posthumous name Zhenjian.
